quantity: fraction of TNF bioactivity (or soluble TNF) neutralised at trough
source: Lenercept MS Study Group & UBC MS/MRI Analysis Group, Neurology 1999;53:457-465 (full text read); Rau et al., J Rheumatol 2003;30:680-690 (full text read)
quote: Trough serum concentrations of lenercept were detectable in only a third of the patients in all dose groups and tended to relate to the anti-lenercept antibody profile.
note: No fetched source states a neutralisation fraction, or complete neutralisation, at trough at 100 mg q4w. The MS trial paper measured only serum lenercept (ELIBA) and anti-lenercept antibodies, no TNF bioactivity or free TNF; it reports trough drug detectable in a third of patients (quote), antibodies in 100% (40/40) of the 100 mg group, and that the antibodies 'do not neutralize TNF binding' but 'accelerate elimination of the drug'. Nearest statement, NOT entered: Rau 2003 (RA, max 0.5 mg/kg = 50 mg q4w): 'comparison of immunoassay results with those of a cytotoxicity assay, measuring only bioactive TNF-alpha, revealed that the TNF-alpha circulating after a dose of Ro 45-2081 was not bioactive. At least initially it was thought that there was a large excess of lenercept to TNF so that nearly all circulating TNF-alpha was bound in a stable and bioinactive fashion.' Rejected as the anchor because it is not a trough statement, is hedged ('at least initially'), is at half the dose in another disease, and the MS paper reports undetectable trough drug in two thirds of patients. If the registrant accepts it as a statement of complete neutralisation the entry would be 0.95. Also read: Furst 2003 J Rheumatol 30:2123 (PK/PD analyses not completed); abstracts of Abraham 1997 JAMA and Abraham 2001 Crit Care Med (sepsis, single dose: 'bound in a stable manner', no fraction). Not retrievable: Sander et al. and Furst et al., Arthritis Rheum 1996;39(suppl 9):S242-243 ('Neutralization of TNF by lenercept', meeting abstracts). The one-third figure is a share of patients, not a neutralisation fraction, and was not converted. No clinical or MRI outcome was used.

dose: 50 mg s.c. weekly (MS501-MS507); 5 mg s.c. weekly x4 then monthly (MS601)
timepoint: baseline vs during APL therapy (Table 1 'before therapy' / 'after therapy'); treatment duration differed per patient
source: Bielekova et al., Nature Medicine 2000;6:1167-1175, Table 1 and text p.1169 (full text read via a third-party transcript of the article PDF; publisher page is paywalled)
